solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cairn's barking about noisy weather feature

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the mixed letters go round the next piece
barking means mad, so the letters of Cairn's go wild and are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive S counts here: all six letters C, A, I, R, N, S are used
noisy means loud

explanation.surface: A cairn terrier yapping at a storm brewing overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: A cairn is a small Scottish terrier, so 'barking' sounds like its yapping, but it signals the anagram (giving RAINC-S), and 'about' signals the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey masses of water vapour that bring wet spells are a typical feature of the weather.

clue.text: Suitable letters attached to name after passing English

parts.words: letters attached to name after passing
parts.note: after someone dies, the letters RIP (rest in peace) are put beside their name on a headstone

explanation.surface: Someone deciding which honours are fit to follow a name once a person leaves England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after passing' looks like travelling past England; it means after dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripe for something means ready or fit for it, as in 'ripe for development'.

clue.text: Rugby flanker for Llanelli in pub's smashed

indicators.note: in signals that the rugby letters go inside the pub word

parts.note: a pub is an inn, so pubs give inns
RU is the abbreviation for Rugby Union

indicators.note: a flanker is on the edge, so this takes the end letter of Llanelli

explanation.surface: A Llanelli rugby flanker gets drunk in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Llanelli is a Welsh rugby town. A flanker is a rugby position, but here it just means an edge letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A building that is in ruins has been wrecked, which is what smashed means here.

clue.text: Popular jam appeals in middle of night

parts.note: a jam of people is a crowd
appeals are pleas

indicators.note: middle of takes the centre letter of the word night

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a traffic jam pleading for help late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam' looks like preserves or traffic; here it is a crush of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that pleases the masses is popular, an idiom for broad appeal.

clue.text: Career honours sadly don't include Oscar

indicators.note: sadly means badly, poorly done, so the letters are rearranged
don't include means one letter is left out of the word honours

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone sorry that their career honours never included an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' is a verb here, to rush headlong. 'don't include' drops one O from HONOURS, and 'sadly' shuffles HNOURS.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to hurtle forward, and a forward surge or rush is the noun sense.

clue.text: Old partner deserted Welshman — character residing by the Dee?

parts.note: Ivor is a typical Welsh man's name
the letter C, spelt out, sits next to D (spelt dee) in the alphabet

explanation.surface: An ex left behind by a Welshman living on the banks of the River Dee.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee looks like the river on the Welsh border; it is the letter D, and the character beside it in the alphabet is C, written CEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person whose marriage has ended is a former spouse, an old partner.

clue.text: Plaster applied originally in friend's retreat

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the reversed friend
retreat means going backwards, so the friend word is reversed

parts.note: a friend is a bud, a pal

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of applied

explanation.surface: Plaster put on a friend's country retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a hideaway; it reverses BUD to DUB.
explanation.definitionFit: To daub is to smear or plaster something thickly over a surface.

clue.text: Rising artist obtains elite building, which includes this?

definitions.text: Rising artist obtains elite building, which includes this?

indicators.note: obtains means holds, so the artist letters surround the rest
rising in a down clue means the letters read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

indicators.note: building means making or constructing, so the letters of elite are rearranged

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming artist buys a grand building with a studio in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reverses RA to AR, which 'obtains' TELIE, the letters of ELITE rearranged by 'building'.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio or workshop for an artist is an atelier, the sort of room an artist's building would contain.

clue.text: Mole's idyllic location?

parts.note: a mole on the face is a small mark called this, and a lovely scenic place has the same name

explanation.surface: Where a mole, the burrowing animal, would love to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' looks like the animal; it is a skin mark, and the two-word name for it also means a lovely scenic place.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark facial mole, once prized, is called this, and the same phrase names a picturesque place.

clue.text: Golf hole, where there's talk, fine for learner

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter swaps for another

parts.note: a parlour was a room for talking, from French parler, to speak
L is the learner sign on a car
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A golf hole by a clubhouse room where members chat, with a fine for beginners.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole that a good player should take four strokes to complete is a par four golf hole.

clue.text: Word class, meeting in French Academy, leaves here

parts.note: a verb is a class of word, a part of speech
en is French for in

explanation.surface: A class on words meeting at the French Academy, then leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb, departing; it is foliage, so 'leaves here' points to a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Vervain is a garden plant, so leaves are found on it; the definition is cryptic.

clue.text: After which Di and Teri become tidier?

definitions.text: After which Di and Teri become tidier?

parts.words: After which Di and Teri become tidier?
parts.note: the letters of Di and Teri, shuffled around, spell tidier

explanation.surface: Two women, Di and Teri, are made neater after some change.
explanation.walkthrough: It looks like Di and Teri get tidied up; in fact their letters are moved round to spell TIDIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Changing the order of letters is a reordering, and that is what turns these names into the word.

clue.text: At home, loose debris is found in messy trail. Hoover needed?

parts.note: at home means in
dust is loose fine debris

indicators.note: found in means the word is goes inside the scrambled trail
messy means untidy, so the letters of trail are scrambled

explanation.surface: Dust and debris trailed messily through the house, so the vacuum cleaner is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoover' looks like the vacuum cleaner; it is William Hoover, the manufacturer. 'messy' gives RIALT and 'found in' does the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hoover built a manufacturing business, so he is an example of a business magnate.

clue.text: Joey returned cross-dressing attire in bog — where bloomers seen?

parts.note: a joey is a young kangaroo, a roo

indicators.note: in places the reversed attire inside the bog word

parts.note: a fen is a bog

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the attire word is read backwards

parts.note: drag is women's clothing worn by a man

explanation.surface: A young kangaroo in drag, stuck in a bog, wearing bloomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like underwear, fitting the drag; it means flowers. 'returned' turns DRAG into GARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers bloom on a planted area on top of a building, so bloomers are seen there.

clue.text: Available for purchase in unit: Rushdie 50% off

indicators.note: in signals the shortened name goes inside the unit word

parts.note: one is a unit

indicators.note: 50% off removes half the letters of the first name

parts.note: Salman Rushdie is the novelist

explanation.surface: A Rushdie book in a shop marked down by half.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% off' looks like a discount; it cuts SALMAN to SAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods offered in a shop are able to be bought, which the phrase means.

clue.text: Grizzly members prepare for fight?

parts.note: a grizzly is a bear
arms are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: Grizzly bears limbering up for a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry weapons ready for battle is the idiom, as in the right to carry guns.

clue.text: Touch restaurant attendant, wanting one glass of this?

parts.note: to tap is to touch lightly

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a waiter attends tables in a restaurant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A diner taps the waiter on the arm to ask for a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' looks like desiring a glass; it means without, so I leaves WAITER.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking for ordinary water from the mains rather than bottled is asking for a glass of this.

clue.text: Type of bed worn out in the hands of footballers, with practice

indicators.note: in the hands of means held by, so the worn-out word sits inside

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association
worn out means old
a way is a practice or custom

explanation.surface: A worn-out bed handed to footballers at training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'practice' looks like football training; it means a custom, a way of doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed that can be folded up and put out of sight is a kind of bed.

clue.text: Cat, close to the surging river, comes in dripping

indicators.note: comes in means these letters enter the dripping word

parts.note: dripping is fat from roasting meat, like lard

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of the word the
surging means rising, and in a down clue rising means read upwards, reversed

parts.note: the Po is the main river of Italy

explanation.surface: A cat comes indoors soaking wet from the swollen river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dripping' looks like soaking wet; it is cooking fat. 'surging' turns PO into OP.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotted big cat of Africa and Asia is a leopard; the clue gives the general class.

clue.text: Like hippy disc tracks in tone

indicators.note: tracks means follows, so the hippy word and disc come after in

parts.note: taken as written
dig was hippy slang for like, as in I dig it
O is disc-shaped

explanation.surface: A hippy-ish record with tracks in a mellow tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tracks' looks like songs on the disc; it means follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep blue-violet is a shade, and a shade of colour can be called a tone.

clue.text: State assistance raised in local area

indicators.note: in places the raised help word inside the pub

parts.note: a local is a British pub, an inn

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: aid is assistance

explanation.surface: State help being collected in the local area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' looks like an adjective; it is a noun, a British word for your neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty United States, so the answer is an example of a state.

clue.text: Garland's heading for wizard with renewed heart

indicators.note: heading for takes the first letter of wizard
renewed means made over again, so the letters of heart are rearranged

explanation.surface: Judy Garland heading off to see the Wizard of Oz, her heart revived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garland's' looks like Judy Garland of The Wizard of Oz; the 's is just 'is'. 'renewed' turns HEART into REATH.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring of flowers or leaves worn or hung up is a garland.

clue.text: Democrat dealt with Hawaii — snubbed nuclear device

indicators.note: dealt with means handled, like cards dealt out, so the letters are shuffled
snubbed means cut short, so the last letter of Hawaii goes

explanation.surface: A US Democrat dealing with Hawaii snubs a nuclear weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snubbed' looks like ignored; it means docked, cutting HAWAII to HAWAI before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The explosive head of a missile carrying a bomb of fission or fusion is a nuclear device.

clue.text: Some large vodkas knocked back — it may help do the trick

definitions.text: it may help do the trick

indicators.note: knocked back means turned backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
some means only part, so the letters lie within large vodkas

explanation.surface: Someone knocking back large vodkas to help pull off a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking; it reverses the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A white bird is a stage magician's classic prop, produced from a hat or sleeve.

clue.text: Slug blight, latterly severe around centre of Burgundy, is repelled

indicators.note: is repelled means pushed back, so everything is read backwards
latterly takes the end letter of blight
around means the hard word wraps the centre letters

parts.note: severe means hard

indicators.note: centre of takes the middle two letters of Burgundy

explanation.surface: A gardener's slug problem, with Burgundy vineyards hit by blight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slug' looks like the garden pest; it is a swig of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A gulp or swallow of a drink is both a slug and a draught.

clue.text: Silvers, last seen in Bilko around the 1950s (latterly), brings years back

indicators.note: around means these letters wrap the next ones

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver, so silvers gives it twice

indicators.note: latterly takes the end letters of the and 1950s
last seen in takes the final letter of Bilko

explanation.surface: Phil Silvers as Sergeant Bilko, the 1950s TV comedy, brings back the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: Phil Silvers played Sergeant Bilko on 1950s TV, but here 'Silvers' is the chemical symbol for the metal, taken twice; 'around' wraps the end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A long time in the past is many years back, an everyday idiom.

clue.text: A desperate chap, comically overcoming zip

indicators.note: overcoming means turning over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Desperate Dan is a strongman character in the British comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A desperate man, comically, beating a zip that has stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is the cowboy hero of the British children's comic The Dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Zip and nada are both slang for nothing at all.

clue.text: Frame Alistair, vacuously taking tab at party

indicators.note: vacuously means emptily, so only the outer letters of Alistair are kept

parts.note: a chit is a tab or bill
a rave is a party

explanation.surface: Framing Alistair, who mindlessly runs up a bar tab at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frame' looks like stitching someone up; it is a moulding round a door.
explanation.definitionFit: The moulded surround of a doorway or window is a frame in architecture.
